speaker: Doctor

I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to help me determine the cause, have you experienced any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in your ear alongside this spinning sensation?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Within normal limits for age.

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

While the previous provider suggested gastroenteritis, your denial of hearing loss and neurological deficits points toward a vestibular cause rather than an inner ear infection or stroke. Since you have no headaches or hearing changes, BPPV is the most likely diagnosis. Did your dizziness start specifically when you changed your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?
